column1: # The runner-health floors (AGENTS.md §11.2; docs/PROOFS.md §5, §10). Every
# CI part measures its runner for about ten seconds before any gate
# (`proofrun runner-health`, run first by scripts/proof-part.sh) and writes
# runner-health.json: the values, these floors, and a verdict. A stack part
# (integration, ui-e2e, activity-fixture, observability) whose runner is
# below a floor of its class stops before any gate, and the merger
# classifies it runner-degraded, exactly as a part whose runner GitHub
# lost: its tests get no outcome of the tree, the proof is not a proof of
# the tree, and that one job may run again. A part above every floor whose
# tests fail is a test failure. A local proof measures the same numbers for
# information only; its class, `local`, has no row here, because the host's
# floors are its measured costs themselves.
# This is a measurement file, like scripts/proof-test-costs.tsv: a feature
# proof may change it (scripts/proof-scope.tsv), and it is NEVER edited to
# get a proof through. A floor can only turn a result into "not a proof of
# the tree"; it never passes one. A class's floors are derived from the
# runner-health.json of every part of healthy CI runs: each floor is well
# under the least healthy measurement (a throughput or a capacity) or well
# over the largest (a latency), with the margin and the runs named in the
# derived column (docs/PROOFS.md §10, "Re-derive the runner-health floors").
# A class with no row is `unfloored`: its parts measure for information, and
# their runner_health in the merged proof.json is the data its rows come
# from. Re-derive a class when more runs widen its range.
# A class is `github-hosted/<ImageOS>/<N>cpu` on a GitHub-hosted runner
# (scripts/proof-part.sh part_runner_class): the runner image and its vCPU
# count, because the all-core and memory floors depend on the runner's size.
# The metrics are the ones `proofrun runner-health` measures, in its order;
# a `_ms` metric is a latency, below its floor when the value is ABOVE it.
# Columns are TAB-separated: class, metric, floor, derived.
